html:
The Dzungar Khanate was the empire of the Oirats, or western Mongols, centred in Dzungaria in what is now northern Xinjiang, from the 1630s to 1758. It was the last great nomadic empire of the steppe.

The Oirats had long been rivals of the eastern Mongols. Around 1620 they united in the Junggar Basin, and the Dzungar tribe came to lead them. The Dzungars were Tibetan Buddhists of the Gelug school and close to the Dalai Lamas. In 1678 the 5th Dalai Lama gave the title of khan to their ruler Galdan.

Under Galdan and his successors the Dzungars:

  • conquered the Tarim Basin oases in 1680 to 1688
  • attacked the Khalkha Mongols in the east, who then turned to the Qing for help
  • raided the Kazakhs for decades, above all in the great invasion of 1723
  • took Lhasa in 1717, until the Qing drove them out in 1720

The Qing saw them as the main threat to their empire. The Kangxi Emperor led armies against Galdan himself and beat him at Jao Modo in 1696.

The end came in a civil war after 1745. The Qianlong Emperor used it to invade, and in 1755 to 1758 Qing armies destroyed the Dzungars. Most of the people were killed in war, by smallpox or by deliberate slaughter, or fled. Historians call it a genocide.

Dzungaria and the Tarim Basin became the Qing province of Xinjiang. The fall of the Dzungars, with Russia advancing from the north, ended two thousand years of steppe empires, a shift the chart marks as gunpowder ends nomad power.
